description: The bar chart illustrates the % point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance across layers of two multilingual BERT models — mBERT (top panel) and XLM-R (bottom panel) — as reported in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis represents model layers, labeled from 0 to 12, followed by “concat,” indicating a concatenated representation of all layers. The vertical axis shows the percentage point difference, ranging from 0 to –10, with negative values indicating a performance drop relative to a baseline. In both models, early layers (0–5) exhibit the largest negative differences, with layer 0 showing the most substantial drop (approximately –10% for both models). Performance differences become smaller and less negative in later layers (6–12), with some layers (e.g., 9, 10, 11) showing near-zero or slightly positive differences. The “concat” layer shows a small positive difference in both models. The mBERT bars are light blue, while XLM-R bars are dark blue, allowing visual comparison between models. The chart suggests that early layers contribute most to the performance gap, while later and concatenated layers are closer to or exceed baseline performance.
